title: Rigveda 1.86: To the Maruts
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 1.86: To the Maruts: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 1.86 is a hymn of 10 verses addressed to the Maruts. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 1, a collection of hymns by many families of poets. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 58v-59r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 1.86.1-3 (aṣṭaka 1, adhyāya 6, varga 11); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 58v
translation.original_text:
1maru̍to̱ yasya̱ hi kṣaye̍ pā̱thā di̱vo vi̍mahasaḥ | sa su̍go̱pāta̍mo̱ jana̍ḥ ||
2ya̱jñair vā̍ yajñavāhaso̱ vipra̍sya vā matī̱nām | maru̍taḥ śṛṇu̱tā hava̍m ||
3u̱ta vā̱ yasya̍ vā̱jino 'nu̱ vipra̱m ata̍kṣata | sa gantā̱ goma̍ti vra̱je ||
translation.text:
1THE best of guardians hath that man within whose dwelling place ye drink, O Maruts, giants of the sky.
2Honoured with sacrifice or with the worship of the sages' hymns, O Maruts, listen to the call.
3Yea, the strong man to whom ye have vouchsafed to give a sage, shall move Into a stable rich in kine.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 58v (OPenn image 60, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 1.85.8 ‹-rājānaḥ-iva tveṣa-sandṛśaḥ naraḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 59r, begins in RV 1.86.4 ‹barhiṣi sutaḥ somaḥ diviṣṭiṣu›. Verses 1.86.1-3 end on this page.
translation.edition_text:
1marutaḥ | yasya | hi | kṣaye | pātha | divaḥ | vi-mahasaḥ | saḥ | su-gopātamaḥ | janaḥ
2yajñaiḥ | vā | yajña-vāhasaḥ | viprasya | vā | matīnām | marutaḥ | śṛṇuta | havam
3uta | vā | yasya | vājinaḥ | anu | vipram | atakṣata | saḥ | gantā | go--mati | vraje

translation.original_ref: RV 1.86.4-10 (aṣṭaka 1, adhyāya 6, varga 11); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 59r
translation.original_text:
4a̱sya vī̱rasya̍ ba̱rhiṣi̍ su̱taḥ somo̱ divi̍ṣṭiṣu | u̱ktham mada̍ś ca śasyate ||
5a̱sya śro̍ṣa̱ntv ā bhuvo̱ viśvā̱ yaś ca̍rṣa̱ṇīr a̱bhi | sūra̍ṁ cit sa̱sruṣī̱r iṣa̍ḥ ||
6pū̱rvībhi̱r hi da̍dāśi̱ma śa̱radbhi̍r maruto va̱yam | avo̍bhiś carṣaṇī̱nām ||
7su̱bhaga̱ḥ sa pra̍yajyavo̱ maru̍to astu̱ martya̍ḥ | yasya̱ prayā̍ṁsi̱ parṣa̍tha ||
8śa̱śa̱mā̱nasya̍ vā nara̱ḥ sveda̍sya satyaśavasaḥ | vi̱dā kāma̍sya̱ vena̍taḥ ||
9yū̱yaṁ tat sa̍tyaśavasa ā̱viṣ ka̍rta mahitva̱nā | vidhya̍tā vi̱dyutā̱ rakṣa̍ḥ ||
10gūha̍tā̱ guhya̱ṁ tamo̱ vi yā̍ta̱ viśva̍m a̱triṇa̍m | jyoti̍ṣ kartā̱ yad u̱śmasi̍ ||
translation.text:
4Upon this hero's sacred grass Soma is poured in daily rites: Praise and delight are sung aloud.
5Let the strong Maruts hear him, him surpassing all men: strength be his That reaches even to the Sun.
6For, through the swift Gods' loving help, in many an autumn, Maruts, we Have offered up our sacrifice.
7Fortunate shall that mortal be, O Maruts most adorable, Whose offerings ye bear away.
8O Heroes truly strong, ye know the toil of him who sings your praise, The heart's desire of him who loves.
9O ye of true strength, make this thing manifest by your greatness – strike The demon with your thunderbolt.
10Conceal the horrid darkness, drive far from us each devouring fiend. Create the light for which we long.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 59r (OPenn image 60, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 1.86.4 ‹barhiṣi sutaḥ somaḥ diviṣṭiṣu›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 59v, begins in RV 1.87.2 ‹-arcate›. Verses 1.86.4-10 end on this page; 1.86.4 begins on fol. 58v.
